ing: enough water to cover the ingredients with an extra 5cm of liquid
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Heat the oil over a medium heat in a large pot. Add the shin to the pot and allow the meat to brown for 4-5 minutes before turning over and cooking the other side in the same manner.

Remove the meat form the pot and set aside before adding the onions and cooking until softened, adding extra oil if needed. Add the remaining vegetable and cook for another 20 minutes or until completely softened.
Return the meat to the pot then add the herbs and seasoning. Spoon in the tomato paste and add the water before pouring in the water and mixing all together.

Reduce the heat to low and simmer with the lid on for 2-3 hours or until the meat begins pulling from the bone. Alternatively place the pot with the lid on in the oven to slowly cook at 160Â°C for the same amount of time.
Allow the Ragu to cool in the pot with the lid on before dividing into 3 using a container with an airtight lid.
Serving option 1:Served over perfectly cooked taglietelle with freshly shaved Parmesan
Serving option 2:Served on a bun as a new take on a sloppy joe
Serving option 3:Served as a pot pie with Woolies All butter puff pastry.
Using a stick blender or a food processor: Blend the bananas and eggs together to form a smooth mixture.

Heat a non-stick pan over a medium heat before greasing with non-stick spray. Add 2-3 tablespoons of the mixture to the pan to form a pancake. Allow the mixture to cook without trying to move it until small bubbles form on the top.
Carefully turn over and cook the pancakes for another 1 minute. Cook the remaining batter in the same manner.

For the topping: Heat the coconut oil over a medium heat before adding the raw trail mix and cook until toasted and fragrant. Add the cinnamon and toss through. Add some of the yoghurt between the layers of pancakes and top with the cinnamon crumble.

t: 3 top tips to marinate your meat
st: Place the chicken into the marinade bag and allow to stand for 1 hour, or even better, overnight.

Heat a griddle pan on the stove. Cook the chicken breasts on either side for 3 minutes, then finish the cooking process in the oven for 8 minutes on 180Â°C. If cooking on the braai, continue until cooked through. Baste with the marinade while braaing.
Serve with Woolworths Herb Salad tossed with sliced radish, exotic tomatoes and shaved carrot, dressed with readymade dressing â we love thebasil and white balsamic dressing.

ing: 500 ml long life cream, chilled overnight and whipped (but you could also use fresh cream and it might take less time to whip)
caramel Swiss roll, cut into slices
st: Mix half of all the beries (except the cherries) into the prepared jelly. Pour into a trifle bowl and leave to set in the fridge.

To make the white chocolate stars or chards, melt chocolate and spread about 2 mm thick over a baking tray lined with grease-proof paper. Sprinkle the chocolate with the Christmas sprinkles and gold shimmer. Place in the fridge to set until ready to serve. Cut out stars with cookie cutter or break into shards.

When ready to serve, spoon the custard in over the jelly and arrange slices ofSwiss rollon top. Add dollops of cream and decorate with cherries, white chocolate stars, edible gold shimmer andChucklesrolled in gold shimmer. Enjoy!
TIP: If it's a hot day, keep the chocolate stars in the fridge until just before serving to ensure they don't melt on the way to the table.

Toast over a low gas flame or medium coals, flipping the jaffle iron every 10 seconds for even toasting and to prevent burning. Toast for 1-2 minutes, then carefully open using gloves to check whether itâs toasted to your liking. Be sure to let an adult do this so the little ones donât burn their hands.
Serve once cooled slightly but still oozy. These are delicious with a mocha or hot chocolate for dunking.

st: Preheat the oven to 200Â°C. Slice potatoes into wafer-thin slices â use a mandolin if you have one. Toss the potato slices in olive oil to coat. Arrange on two baking trays lined with baking paper, making sure the potatoes donât overlap. Sprinkle with sea salt and bake for 15â20 minutes, or until golden.
